## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Make `--exclude` read its default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` so CI jobs can omit matching files through their environment.

## Changes
The PR adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag that matches file basenames and logs skipped files in verbose mode. It also adds flag documentation, tests, and a text fixture.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` — With `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` and no explicit `--exclude`, the CLI archives `build.log` because the parser defaults to `[]`. `.agents/skills/cli-flags/reference.md:5` says each new flag “must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable.” — CI jobs can ship archives containing files they configured the tool to omit.

## Suggestions
- tests/test_main.py:18 — tests — Verify both exclusions in the resulting archive — For `--exclude '*.log' --exclude '*.tmp'`, the test checks the parser’s list and would still pass if `main` forwarded only the first pattern. The archive test supplies one pattern. — A regression that drops the second exclusion could leave matching files in the archive while all tests pass.
- cli/main.py:33 — tests — Test a literal basename in a nested directory — No test supplies `--exclude skip.log` for a file such as `subdir/skip.log`. The existing wildcard patterns would also match full paths, so the tests would pass if this call matched `path`. — A regression to full-path matching could archive nested files that users exclude by basename.
